title: Rosie's Mitten Mission
markdown:
It was a super-duper sparkly morning. The snow went *crunch-crunch-crunch* under Rosie’s feet. Everything looked like it had sugar sprinkled on top. Sparkly sunbeams danced on the trees. They twinkled like little jewels.

Rosie the Rabbit was a fluffy ball of bouncy energy. Her ears could hear a whisper from far, far away. *Boing! Boing! Boing!* She wore her favorite blue boots. They had fluffy pom-poms that bounced with every hop. The boots made her feel super zippy.

Suddenly, Rosie’s nose twitched. She smelled something fuzzy. It wasn’t her own fluff! It smelled a little like warm wool. And maybe a little like… adventure! She hopped closer. Her ears flopped forward like little questions. Her bright eyes looked at the snowy ground. And there it was! Tucked in the snow, looking all alone, was a bright red mitten. It was a perfect red mitten. It would make fingers feel super warm.

"Oh my whiskers!" squeaked Rosie. "A mitten! A lost mitten! It looks so sad by itself!" She thought about someone’s little hand feeling very cold.

Then, who came trundling by? Toby the Turtle. Toby walked slowly. His shell was the color of warm caramel. It smelled like sunshine and damp earth. He moved slowly, like a sleepy snail. But he saw *everything*.

"Hullo, Rosie!" said Toby. His voice was gentle, like a soft breeze. "What have you found?"

"A mitten, Toby! A bright red, lonely, lost mitten!" Rosie bounced. Her pom-pom boots jiggled. "Someone must be sad! Their fingers must be chilly-chilly-chilly!"

Toby blinked his wise, slow eyes. "Indeed. And look!" He pointed with his nose. "Tiny footprints! See? *Pat-pat-pat.* They go that way!" He pointed to little prints in the snow. They looked like tiny stamps. They headed into the snowy woods.

Rosie’s ears perked up. They nearly touched the sky. She wiggled with excitement. "Footprints! Oh, Toby! We can follow them! We can find the mitten’s owner! We can give it back! It’ll be an adventure! A *Mitten Mission*!"

Toby smiled his slow, steady smile. "An adventure it is. But Rosie, I do not hop like you. My walk is more of a… *wobble-wobble*."

"That’s okay!" Rosie giggled. Her tail gave a happy flick. "I can hop ahead and hop back! You can tell me what you see!"

And so, the Great Mitten Mission began! Rosie held the red mitten. She took a big hop. *Boing!* Toby followed with a slow wiggle. *Wobble-wobble.* The footprints went *pat-pat-pat*. Rosie followed the *pat-pat-pat*.

They walked past a garden gnome statue. He looked sleepy. He had a long white beard. Rosie thought his painted eyes winked at her. *Wink!* Rosie giggled. Toby blinked. "Gnomes don't wink, Rosie," he said softly.

Then, they came to a bouncy bush. *Whoa-ho-ho!* The bush seemed to wiggle. It swayed like a dancer. Rosie nudged it with her nose. *Boing!* The bush bounced her onto Toby’s back! "Wheee!" she cried. Her ears flapped. Toby chuckled. A low rumble, like a pebble rolling downhill. His shell was strong.

They followed the *pat-pat-pat* footprints to some tall, fluffy dandelions. And oh my goodness! Tucked under a snoozing badger was another bright red mitten! The other one! It was the same as the first.

Rosie gasped. "The other mitten! It’s right there!" She started to hop forward. Her ears twitched. "We found both! Oh, Toby, this is amazing!"

"Shhh!" Toby whispered. He put a little turtle finger to his lips. "The badger is sleeping. If we wake him, he might be very… *grumbly*. No one likes a grumbly badger." Rosie looked at the badger. He had a snoozing smile. His snores were getting louder. She didn’t want to make him *grumbly*. Not at all.

Rosie thought hard. Her nose twitched. Then, she had an idea! A super-duper, clever idea! She felt a little tingle down to her boots. She tiptoed very, very carefully towards the badger. *Tiptoe-tiptoe-tiptoe.* Her blue boots made no sound. She reached out her paw. She scooped up a soft, fluffy bit of snow right next to the badger’s nose. Then, she tiptoed back to Toby.

"Okay, Toby," she whispered. Her voice was a tiny rustle of snow. "You are the calmest. Can you hold this snow carefully? I'll tiptoe over there. When I get the mitten, I'll tiptoe back. We’ll leave the snow. Maybe he’ll think it was just snow falling!"

Toby nodded. His eyes were wide. He carefully held a fluffy snowball. Rosie crept, *tiptoe-tiptoe-tiptoe*, past the badger’s nose. The snow felt cold on her paws. She could smell the badger’s cozy, earthy smell. Like warm blankets. She gently, oh so gently, scooped up the second red mitten. Then, she tiptoed back, *tiptoe-tiptoe-tiptoe*, back to Toby.

"We did it!" she whispered. She held both mittens. Toby let out a tiny sigh of relief. The badger snoozed on. His snores sounded like a gentle *whoosh-whoosh*.

The footprints *pat-pat-patted* a little further. They led to a tiny cottage. It had a chimney puffing out happy little curls of smoke. Little icicles hung like tiny ice chandeliers. Peeking out from behind a curtain was a little squirrel. He had a hopeful look. His whiskers drooped a tiny bit.

Rosie and Toby tiptoed to the little wooden door. Rosie tapped. *Tap-tap-tap.*

The door opened. There stood the little squirrel! His eyes lit up like Christmas lights. "My mittens!" he squeaked. His voice was full of joy. "Oh, thank you! Thank you! My fingers were getting so cold. They felt like tiny icicles!" He took the mittens. He wiggled his fingers. "Now they’re warm and cozy!"

He looked at Rosie and Toby. His bushy tail twitched. "You are the kindest friends! Come in, come in! You must be cold!"

Inside, the cottage was warm. It smelled like cinnamon and sunshine and bread. The little squirrel, Squeaky, poured them cups of warm apple cider. It was sweet and tasted like autumn. And guess what? He brought out warm, nutty, delicious cookies. Rosie’s tummy did a happy wiggle. Toby’s shell hummed.

Rosie and Toby sat, munching cookies and sipping cider. They had followed the footprints. They had been brave. They had been clever. They had made a new friend. Helping someone feel warm and happy felt even better than the best cookie. It felt like a warm hug.

Rosie looked at Toby. Toby looked at Rosie. They didn’t need to say anything. They knew it was a perfect end to their adventure. They had done it all together. With a bounce and a wobble. And a whole lot of kindness. They were the bestest of friends. And that was the warmest feeling of all.
characters: Rosie the rabbit, Toby the turtle
author: StoryGen Community
